title: Chapter 6. The Five Elements, the Three States, and the Great Artist of the Universe

blocks.text: The Teacher told his students: this world looks solid, and matter feels firm. But really, everything is made of moving streams. It looks permanent, but it's woven out of constant change. It looks like many separate things, but it all comes from the same source.
This is how he revealed to his students the secret of the Elements of Existence.
The World Is Woven from Five Elements

Every visible form is just a mix of five basics: earth, water, fire, air, and space. Earth gives stability. Water gives flow. Fire gives the power to transform. Air gives movement. Space gives room for everything — the power to expand.
These five elements meet and weave together in every object we can see and touch — and in each of us too.
Beyond the Five Elements
The Teacher said time is the breath of the universe, space is its body, atoms are its syllables, and forms are its words.

Time joins atoms into crystals and molecules, then later unravels bodies, like threads of aging cloth. It grows a leaf, then turns it yellow and lets it fall. It brings children into this world, and it leads the old ones away.
"No one can defeat time. But a wise person learns to move with it," said the teacher. "Time is not an enemy. It shows us the Source."
The Alphabet of Being — Twenty-Four Elements
The students were surprised. Weren't five elements enough? The teacher said there are twenty-four basic parts of existence, but they all come from one root.
Besides the five elements and time, there is the mind, the senses, the organs of perception, the organs of action, and matter in its subtle and gross forms.
The whole world is built from these, just as complex writing is built from simple strokes, music from seven notes, and a painting from three colors, darkness, and light.
Three States: Goodness, Passion, and Ignorance
The teacher said again that everything in this visible world is always colored by three states, called gunas: goodness, passion, and ignorance.
That's why the same action can bring different results, and the same things can look different to different people. We act from different states of mind, and we see things through different eyes.
Every thought, every action, and every choice is a mix of these three gunas. But whoever understands their true nature becomes free.
"Whoever sees the colors stops being a color. Whoever sees the states stops belonging to them."
A master calmly watches desires move, emotions rise and fall, and the mind grow restless. All of this is just the play of the three gunas. He does not mistake himself for any of them.
A wise person is like a mirror. It reflects things, but it never touches what it reflects.
The Great Artist

The teacher pointed to the sunset glowing on the horizon. He said there is a great Artist who mixes the first colors of all worlds. And there are small artists — living beings who paint their own pictures and think they created everything themselves.
The difference is only in scale, not in nature. The Great Artist creates the universe. The small one creates his own life. But both create. A spark of His creative power lives in every soul.
Knowing the Elements Brings Peace to the Heart

Elements move, states mix together, time keeps going, forms are born and then disappear. A wise person understands: peace does not come from the world standing still. It comes from understanding how the world truly works.
The teacher said that whoever understands the nature of the elements also understands how he is different from them.
And once he sees this difference, he starts to seek the one who stands above all elements.
Elements come and go. Their states keep changing. Time never stops moving. Space itself passes away.
But the one who made these laws, who keeps them running, and who touches the heart of every being — He never dies.
The point of knowledge is not to control the world, but to love the Source of the world. This is how true devotion is born — devotion that leads the soul back home, to the light it came from.
